hook: Train your ear for academic German, from long genitive chains to giant compounds, so you can write down a lecture sentence correctly.
intro: Twelve sentences of academic German, dictated. They contain exactly the features that trip up the ear in formal texts: genitive chains (die Auswertung der Ergebnisse der Untersuchung; die Kosten des Verfahrens; die Zahl der Teilnehmenden; der Bericht des Forschungsteams), compounds with and without a linking -s- (Forschungsergebnisse, Prüfungsordnung, Auswertungsverfahren, Universitätsleitung, Semesterende), the formal prepositions that announce a genitive (hinsichtlich, angesichts, mangels, seitens, zwecks) and laut with a bare noun (laut Prüfungsordnung), passive substitutes (ist einzureichen, sind vorzulegen, lässt sich überprüfen, lässt sich erkennen) and two participial clauses set off by a comma (Von den Ergebnissen überrascht, …; Kurz vor Semesterende veröffentlicht, …). Type each sentence after hearing it whole; the article at the start of a noun phrase tells you the case of everything that follows.
tips[0].title: Hear the genitive chain
tips[0].text: die Auswertung der Ergebnisse der Untersuchung — three nouns, two genitives. Write the article you hear (der, des) and the -s or -es on masculine and neuter nouns (des Verfahrens, des Experiments, des Forschungsteams).
tips[0].check.why: das Experiment in the genitive is des Experiments; the -s on the noun confirms the article you hear.
tips[1].title: Compounds: one word, with or without Fugen-s
tips[1].text: Forschungsergebnisse, Prüfungsordnung, Auswertungsverfahren, Universitätsleitung — nouns in -ung, -heit, -keit, -ität take the linking -s- when they come first; Semesterende and Fachzeitschrift have none. Spoken as one stressed unit, written as one word.
tips[1].check.why: Nouns in -ität take a linking -s- when they come first, and the compound is written as one word.
tips[2].title: Formal prepositions announce a genitive
tips[2].text: hinsichtlich, angesichts, mangels, seitens, zwecks, ungeachtet — when you hear one, the next article is des / der, or (without an article) the noun stands bare: zwecks Überprüfung, laut Prüfungsordnung.
tips[2].check.why: angesichts takes the genitive, and the genitive plural article is der.
tips[3].title: The comma after a participial group
tips[3].text: A participial group at the start (Von den Ergebnissen überrascht) is usually followed by a comma in careful writing; the main clause then continues with the finite verb.
tips[3].check.why: The comma closes the whole participial group; then the main clause starts with the finite verb.
remember[0]: Article first, case follows; -s / -es on masculine and neuter genitives.
remember[1]: Compounds are one word; formal prepositions take the genitive; a participial group is followed by a comma.
exam: In the C1 exam, accurate genitives, compounds and formal prepositions count in writing — dictation trains exactly that spelling.
